title: Second Reading of the IMDA (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on a Bill to amend the Info-communications Media Development Authority Act and make related amendments to the Telecommunications Act, aligning media-sector regulation with telecommunications regulation.
why_it_matters: The Bill would require IMDA approval for acquisitions of 30% or more of a regulated media entity and allow IMDA to issue directions on market conduct and consumer protection. It would also allow the Minister to order structural separation as a last resort. The record does not set out specific price, service or employment outcomes.

key_points.point: The Bill aligns the media-sector regulatory framework with the telecommunication sector.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Principally, the amendments align the regulatory framework for the media sector with that for the telecommunication sector.

key_points.point: Under the amended ownership framework, IMDA prior approval would apply where a person acquires 30% or more interest, obtains effective control, or takes over a media business as a going concern.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Specifically, this would apply where a person acquires 30% or more interest in a regulated person, obtains effective control over its operations, or takes over its media business as a going concern.

key_points.point: Clause 6 empowers IMDA to issue directions for fair and efficient market conduct or to safeguard consumers' interests.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Clause 6 of the Bill empowers IMDA to issue directions for the purposes of maintaining fair and efficient market conduct or to safeguard consumers' interests by promoting fair, transparent and reliable provision of media services.

key_points.point: Clause 15 vests the power to order structural separation in the Minister rather than IMDA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: clause 15 provides that the powers to order structural separation of a regulated person is vested in the Minister rather than IMDA.

key_points.point: Clause 3 updates the definition of parties who can be designated as regulated persons.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: clause 3 updates the definition of parties who can be designated as regulated persons to address potential gaps.

key_points.point: Clause 5 allows IMDA to approve documents prepared by a person other than IMDA as a code of practice or standard of performance.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: clause 5 allows IMDA to approve documents prepared by a person other than IMDA as a code of practice or standard of performance for the media sector.

key_points.point: The amendment for immaterial transactions is intended to lighten the regulatory burden and align with the telecom sector.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: This amendment will lighten the regulatory burden and align the approach taken for the telecom sector.

key_points.point: Clause 18 makes related amendments to the Telecommunications Act for alignment purposes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: clause 18 makes related amendments to the Telecommunications Act itself.

key_points.point: Mr Sharael Taha supported the Bill to strengthen competition, protect consumers and keep the media ecosystem fair, vibrant and resilient.
key_points.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
key_points.quote: I rise in support of this Bill to strengthen competition, protect consumers and ensure that our media ecosystem remains fair, vibrant and resilient.

key_points.point: Mr Sharael Taha said that broader regulatory powers require clearer guardrails.
key_points.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
key_points.quote: When regulatory powers become broader, the guardrails must become clearer.

key_points.point: Mr Sharael Taha described the Bill as moving from regulating behaviour to shaping market structure.
key_points.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
key_points.quote: We are moving from regulating behaviour to shaping market structure itself or potentially shaping market itself.

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi called the Bill a necessary and timely update to harmonise regulations in a converging digital market.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: The Bill is a necessary and timely update to harmonise regulations within a converging digital market.

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi noted that clause 15 vests the power to issue a separation order directly in the Minister rather than IMDA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: One change in the Bill is clause 15, which amends the law to vest the power to issue a separation order, which can require a company to restructure or divest parts of its business to address competition concerns, directly in the Minister rather than IMDA.

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi said the Bill does not currently require detailed publication of reasons for such decisions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: The Bill does not currently require the detailed publication of reasons for such decisions.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng supported the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: I support this Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng said competition policy must reduce prices families feel, not just rearrange ownership.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: Competition policy must not just rearrange ownership. It must reduce prices that families actually feel.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how IMDA will work with MOM and unions to support workers affected by restructuring.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: Can the Minister clarify how IMDA will work with MOM and unions to ensure that workers affected by such changes are adequately supported and that transitions are managed fairly?

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre said the Workers' Party does not dispute the administrative case for the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: The Workers' Party does not dispute the administrative case for this Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre identified three significant new powers: proactive directions, ownership approval and Ministerial separation orders.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: The Bill introduces three significant new powers: a proactive directions regime under the new section 61A, an ownership approval regime under the new section 65 and the Ministerial separation order under new section 69A.

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre said the Minister can designate any newspaper publisher or broadcaster as a regulated person on no published criteria.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: The Minister can designate any newspaper publisher or broadcaster as a "regulated person" on no published criteria and bring the full weight of this regime to bear.

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre said he had six questions for the Senior Minister of State.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: So, I have six questions for the Senior Minister of State.

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling supported the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: I support this Bill.

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling asked how IMDA will distinguish between capability-enhancing investment, concentration risk and longer-term dependency creation.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: The key implementation question is this: how will IMDA distinguish between capability-enhancing investment, competitive concentration risk and longer-term dependency creation within the ecosystem?

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling asked whether the Ministry will set out broad guiding principles on when structural separation is appropriate.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: Will the Ministry set out broad guiding principles on when structural separation is considered appropriate?

key_points.point: Dr Hamid Razak supported the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
key_points.quote: I rise in support of the IMDA (Amendment) Bill.

key_points.point: Dr Hamid Razak asked what procedural safeguards will apply to the new direction power, such as notice, representations and review avenues.
key_points.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
key_points.quote: On the new power to issue directions for fair and efficient market conduct, can the Senior Minister of State clarify what procedural safeguards will apply where practicable, such as notice, representations and review avenues, so that speed is balanced with due process?

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan supported the intent of the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: I support the intent of the Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan noted that IMDA must give prior approval before any party acquires a 30% or larger stake in a regulated media company.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: Under this Bill, IMDA must give prior approval before any party acquires a 30% or larger stake in a regulated media company.

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan said the powers should be exercised in a pro-competition and pro-worker way.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: It is important that the powers in this Bill are exercised in ways that are pro-competition and pro-worker, so that a "market win" does not become a "social loss".

key_points.point: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo supported the Bill as helping Singapore keep pace with digital and media changes.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
key_points.quote: I support this Bill because it will help Singapore keep pace with how quickly the digital and media world is evolving.

key_points.point: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo said section 61A strengthens fair access to essential resources such as content libraries, distribution platforms and advertising inventories.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
key_points.quote: The new section 61A strengthens fair access to essential resources, such as content libraries, distribution platforms and advertising inventories.

key_points.point: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo said section 72A requires IMDA approval once a party crosses the 30% ownership threshold.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
key_points.quote: Section 72A ensures that large acquisitions cannot take place quietly or without scrutiny, it requires IMDA's approval once a party crosses the 30% ownership threshold

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe spoke in support of the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: I am speaking in support of the IMDA (Amendment) Bill.

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe said an open and contestable media ecosystem should in principle create more opportunities.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: A media ecosystem that is open and contestable should, in principle, create more opportunities.

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe asked whether IMDA will publish clear decision frameworks or guidelines on how key concepts will be applied.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: Will IMDA also publish clear decision frameworks or guidelines on how these concepts will be applied?

not_said: Whether the Government will publish criteria for designating regulated persons before any designation is made.
Whether the Government will publish criteria for invoking the public interest ground under section 61A.
Whether an independent appeal mechanism on the merits will be adopted.
Whether the Minister will publish detailed reasons for separation orders.
Whether workforce impact will be formally incorporated into IMDA merger assessments.
Whether the expanded definitions will capture ordinary commercial collaborations among smaller players.
Whether the Bill will lead to lower prices or better outcomes for consumers.
Whether the new powers will affect investment in independent media.
What response the Senior Minister of State will give to the questions raised by Members.
